wa_d_waterfall_wall.blurb: Waterfall Wall is a bolted sport face on Mt Washington near North Bend, one of several sub-walls that make up the Upper Wall. It holds ten sport routes, split between a few 5.10s, a couple of 5.11s and a bigger group of 5.12s, so it suits climbers who already lead in the 10 to 12 range rather than beginners. The face is slightly overhanging and fairly tall, with a dark and light streaked section that serves as a landmark. Water runs over it for much of the year, and it tends to be dry only from midsummer into October. Reaching it takes a climb up fixed ropes past the lower walls.

wa_givler_s_dome.blurb: Givler's Dome rises on the north side of Icicle Road in Icicle Canyon, a short drive from Leavenworth, and can be spotted from the roadside pullouts. A pale streak worn by climbers' traffic follows its famous hand crack, which splits the dome in two. Most of the ten climbs here are traditional lines, with a few bolted sport routes, running from easy 5.7 crack climbing up through a handful of 5.10s and 5.11s to one 5.13. Some of the bolted slab routes next to the crack are runout, so top-roping them first is a common tactic. Expect a steady uphill hike of 20 to 25 minutes to reach the base, and a walk-off down the back.

wa_cdc.blurb: CDC is a single stout boulder in the Semantics Area of the Treasury zone in the Skykomish Valley, up near Index and roughly an hour from Seattle. Its ten problems cover a wide range, from a V0 warm-up through the middle grades to several V7 and V8 lines, so it rewards strong climbers more than beginners. Although the boulder is not very tall, every line on it asks something of you. It sits in a shaded grove of trees, which keeps it cool. A short trail leads off to the right just before the Semantics boulder and heads toward the stream.

wa_east_gibralter.blurb: East Gibralter is one section of the Gibralter Rocks, a triangular formation in Northrup Canyon beside Banks Lake in central Washington. It holds ten routes, mostly bolted sport lines with a pair of traditional climbs, including a multi-pitch arete at 5.8. Grades step up from 5.8 through the 5.9s and 5.10s into the 5.11s and 5.12s, so there is something for intermediates and a few lines for stronger leaders. The wider Gibralter Rocks are sunny for most of the day, though a wall at the south end stays in shade until around mid-afternoon. Rock quality across the formation is mixed, with solid sections alongside poorer ones.
